evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/usePushNotifications.ts:223 vs :227 (registerForPushNotifications) — the hook calls `setIsRegistered(true)` at line 223 BEFORE it awaits `sendTokenToBackend(nativeToken.data)` at line 227. sendTokenToBackend posts the device's FCM/APNs token to the api-server (`sendPushTokenToBackend` -> `apiRequest`), which can reject on any backend 4xx/5xx or network error. When it throws, the surrounding catch (line ~230) only does `setError(message); return null;` — it never rolls `isRegistered` back to false.

Consequence: on a backend-registration failure the hook reports `isRegistered === true` (exposed in the returned API at line 315) while the api-server never stored this device's push token. The device therefore silently receives NO pushes, there is NO retry, and any UI gated on `isRegistered` shows a successful/complete registration — a silent, permanent (for the session) delivery failure that masks itself. This defeats the entire purpose of the hook (direct FCM/APNs fan-out).

Reachability: register is the app's push-enrolment entry point; a transient backend outage, an expired/absent access token at enrolment time, or a 4xx from the push-tokens endpoint all trip it under normal operating conditions. Verified net-new against prior mobile-rn signal files and backlog ids.

Suggested fix (implementer): move `setIsRegistered(true)` to AFTER `await sendTokenToBackend(...)` succeeds, so the flag reflects backend acceptance rather than local token acquisition; in the catch, ensure `setIsRegistered(false)` (and optionally surface a retriable error state). Add a jest-expo unit test asserting that when `sendPushTokenToBackend` rejects, the hook ends with `isRegistered === false` and a non-null `error` (satisfies IG3 — fails on current main).

frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/usePushNotifications.ts:154-156 (checkRegistrationStatus) — sets `setIsRegistered(status === 'granted')` purely from `Notifications.getPermissionsAsync()`, i.e. from OS notification-permission state alone, with no knowledge of whether the api-server currently holds this device's push token.

This conflates two distinct facts under one boolean: (a) the user has granted OS notification permission, and (b) the backend can actually deliver pushes to this device (has a current, non-rotated token). On app launch with a previously-granted permission, `isRegistered` becomes true without the current session ever (re)sending the token, so a stale or rotated device token — or a device whose token was never successfully persisted (see sibling finding code-review-mobile-rn-push-isregistered-premature) — is reported as fully registered. Any UI/telemetry that treats `isRegistered` as 'backend will deliver pushes' is misled.

Severity low: this is a semantic-conflation / observability smell rather than a crash; it compounds the premature-flag bug above and makes silent delivery failures harder to detect. Suggested fix: split the concept into `permissionGranted` (OS state) and `backendRegistered` (token successfully persisted this session / confirmed by backend), or re-send the token on launch when permission is granted and only set `backendRegistered` on backend ack.
